summary: Akavya ben Mahalalel teaches that thinking about three things keeps us from sin: where we come from, where we are going, and that one day we will have to stand before Hashem, the King of kings.

chunks.en: Akavya ben Mahalalel says:
Look at three things
and you will not come to sin:
Know where you came from,
and where you are going,
and before Whom you will one day
have to give a judgment and an accounting.
chunks.explain: You will have to explain everything you did.

chunks.en: Where did you come from?
From a smelly drop.
And where are you going?
To a place of dust, worms and maggots.
And before Whom will you one day
have to give a judgment and an accounting?
Before the King of all kings,
the Holy One, blessed is He.

summary: Rabbi Chanina teaches us to daven for the government, because it keeps order. Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon teaches that when people sit together and talk words of Torah, the Shechinah is with them, and even one person who learns alone gets a reward.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, says:
Daven for the peace of the government,
because if not for the fear of it,
people would swallow each other alive.
Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon says:

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין וְאֵין בֵּינֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: Two people who sit and there are no words of Torah between them,
that is a seat of scoffers,
chunks.explain: People who make fun of serious things.

chunks.en: as it says (Tehillim 1): And in the seat
of scoffers he did not sit.
But two who sit
and there are words of Torah between them,
the Shechinah rests among them,
as it says (Malachi 3): Then those who fear

chunks.he: יְיָ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ וַיַּקְשֵׁב יְיָ
chunks.en: Hashem spoke to each other, and Hashem listened,

chunks.he: וַיִּשְׁמָע וַיִּכָּתֵב סֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן לְפָנָיו לְיִרְאֵי
chunks.en: and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear
Hashem and those who think about His Name.

words.en: and for those who think of

chunks.en: This only teaches about two.

chunks.he: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה,
chunks.en: How do we know that even one who sits and learns Torah,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קוֹבֵעַ לוֹ שָׂכָר,
chunks.en: the Holy One, blessed is He, sets a reward for him?
As it says (Eichah 3): He sits alone
and is quiet, because he took it upon himself.

summary: Rabbi Shimon teaches that when three people eat together and say words of Torah, it is as if they ate from Hashem's table. If they do not, it is like eating offerings to idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
Three people who ate at one table
and did not say words of Torah at it,
it is as if they ate from offerings to dead idols,
as it says (Yeshayah 28): For all the tables
are full of a dirty mess, without Hashem.
But three who ate at
one table and said words of Torah at it,
it is as if they ate from the table of
Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Yechezkel 41): And he said to me:
This is the table that is before Hashem.

summary: Rabbi Chanina ben Chachinai warns that being awake at night, walking alone on the road, or letting your mind be empty of Torah puts a person in danger.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Chachinai says:
One who is awake at night, and one who walks on the road
alone, and one who turns his heart to emptiness,
chunks.explain: He thinks about nothing instead of Torah.

chunks.en: he puts his life in danger.

summary: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah teaches that someone who takes on the yoke of Torah is freed from other burdens, but someone who throws off the Torah gets other burdens put on him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah says:
Whoever takes on himself the yoke of Torah,
chunks.explain: A yoke is a wooden bar that lets an animal pull a load.

chunks.en: they remove from him the yoke of the government
and the yoke of earning a living.
And whoever throws off the yoke of Torah,
they put on him the yoke of the government
and the yoke of earning a living.

summary: Rabbi Chalafta teaches that when people learn Torah together, the Shechinah is with them. This is true for ten, five, three, two, and even one person.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chalafta ben Dosa
of Kfar Chananyah says:
Ten people who sit and learn Torah,
the Shechinah rests among them,
as it says (Tehillim 82): Hashem
stands in the assembly of Hashem.
And how do we know even five?
As it says (Amos 9): And His group
He set up on the earth.
And how do we know even three?
As it says (Tehillim 82): Among the judges He judges.
chunks.explain: A beis din has three judges.

chunks.en: And how do we know even two?
As it says (Malachi 3): Then spoke
those who fear Hashem, each to his friend,
and Hashem listened and heard, and so on.
And how do we know even one?
As it says (Shemos 20): In every place where

chunks.he: אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ:
chunks.en: I let My Name be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.

summary: Rabbi Elazar teaches to give to Hashem from what is His, because everything we have belongs to Him. Rabbi Shimon warns not to stop learning Torah to admire nature.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar of Barsosa says:
Give Him from what is His,
because you and what is yours are His.
And so it says about Dovid (Divrei
HaYamim I 29): For from You
comes everything, and from Your hand we gave to You.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who walks on the road and learns,
and stops his learning and says:
How beautiful is this tree!
And how beautiful is this field!

chunks.he: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ מִתְחַיֵּב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ:
chunks.en: the Torah counts it against him as if he put his life in danger.

summary: Rabbi Meir teaches that a person must be very careful not to forget his learning on purpose, but someone who forgets because it was too hard is not to blame.

chunks.en: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai,
in the name of Rabbi Meir, says:
Whoever forgets one thing from his learning,

chunks.he: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ מִתְחַיֵּב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ,
chunks.en: the Torah counts it against him as if he put his life in danger,
as it says (Devarim 4): Only guard yourself

chunks.he: וּשְׁמֹר נַפְשְׁךָ מְאֹד פֶּן תִּשְׁכַּח אֶת
chunks.en: and guard your soul very much, so that you do not forget
the things that your eyes saw.
I might think even if his learning was too hard for him,
so the Torah says (there): And so that they do not leave
your heart all the days of your life.
So he is not guilty
until he sits and removes them from his heart.

summary: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa teaches that wisdom lasts when a person's fear of sin comes first, and when his good deeds are more than his wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa says:
Anyone whose fear of sin comes before his wisdom,
his wisdom will last.
And anyone whose wisdom comes before his fear of sin,
his wisdom will not last.
He used to say:
Anyone whose deeds are more than his wisdom,
his wisdom will last.
And anyone whose wisdom is more than his deeds,
his wisdom will not last.

summary: Rabbi Chanina teaches that if people are pleased with someone, Hashem is pleased with him too. Rabbi Dosa warns that sleeping late, drinking wine at midday, silly talk and sitting with people who don't learn take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Anyone whom people are pleased with,
Hashem is pleased with him.

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵין רוּחַ הַבְּרִיּוֹת נוֹחָה הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: And anyone whom people are not pleased with,
Hashem is not pleased with him.
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
Sleeping late in the morning,
and wine in the middle of the day,
and children's chatter,

chunks.he: וִישִׁיבַת בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: and sitting in the meeting places of unlearned people,
take a person out of the world.

summary: Rabbi Elazar HaModai lists people who lose their share in the World to Come, like one who embarrasses his friend in public, even if he has Torah and good deeds.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar HaModai says:
One who treats holy things as ordinary,
and one who looks down on the Yomim Tovim,

words.en: and the one who looks down on

chunks.en: and one who embarrasses his friend in public,

words.en: and the one who makes white
words.note: Embarrasses, so his face goes pale.

chunks.en: and one who breaks the covenant of Avraham
our father, peace be upon him,
and one who explains the Torah against the halachah,
even though he has
Torah and good deeds in his hand,
he has no share in the World to Come.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches to be quick to serve a great person, to be pleasant to a young person, and to greet everyone happily.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Be quick to serve a leader,
and easy-going with a young person,

words.note: Someone with black hair, not yet gray.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מְקַבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאָדָם בְּשִׂמְחָה:
chunks.en: and greet every person with joy.

summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that joking around leads to bad behavior, and that fences protect good things: tradition protects the Torah, maaser protects wealth, promises protect self-control, and silence protects wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
Joking and lightheadedness
lead a person to forbidden behavior.
The Mesorah is a fence for the Torah.

words.note: The tradition of how the words of the Torah are written.

chunks.en: Maaser is a fence for wealth.
Promises are a fence for holding back.
A fence for wisdom is silence.

summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that Hashem loves people, who were made in His image. He loves the Jewish people, who are called His children and who were given the precious Torah.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Man is dear, because he was created in Hashem's image.

chunks.he: חִבָּה יְתֵרָה נוֹדַעַת לוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְצֶלֶם,
chunks.en: It is an extra love that it was told to him that he was created in Hashem's image,
as it says (Bereishis 9): For in the image
of Hashem He made man.
Yisrael are dear, because they are called Hashem's children.
It is an extra love that it was told to them
that they are called Hashem's children,
as it says (Devarim 14): Children
are you to Hashem your G-d.

chunks.he: חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתַּן לָהֶם כְּלִי חֶמְדָּה.
chunks.en: Yisrael are dear, because they were given a precious tool.

chunks.he: חִבָּה יְתֵרָה נוֹדַעַת לָהֶם שֶׁנִּתַּן לָהֶם
chunks.en: It is an extra love that it was told to them that they were given
a precious tool, with which the world was created,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For
a good teaching I have given you,
do not leave My Torah.

summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that Hashem sees everything, yet we are free to choose. Hashem judges the world with goodness, according to most of our deeds.

chunks.en: Everything is seen,
yet permission is given,
chunks.explain: We are free to choose good or bad.

chunks.en: and the world is judged with goodness.
And everything is by the most of the deeds.

summary: Rabbi Akiva compares the world to a store where everything is given on loan. Hashem keeps track of everything, people are paid back fairly, and at the end, everything is ready for the great feast for the tzaddikim.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Everything is given as a loan with a promise,
and a net is spread over all living things.
The store is open,
and the storekeeper gives credit,
chunks.explain: He lets you take now and pay later.

chunks.en: and the account book is open,
and the hand writes,
and whoever wants to borrow can come and borrow,
and the collectors go around always, every day,

chunks.he: וְנִפְרָעִין מִן הָאָדָם מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and collect from a person whether he knows it or not,
and they have what to lean on,
chunks.explain: They have the account book to show.

chunks.en: and the judgment is a true judgment,
and everything is ready for the feast.

words.note: The reward of the tzaddikim in the World to Come.

summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah teaches that Torah and good manners, wisdom and fear of Hashem, all need each other. Someone whose deeds are more than his wisdom is like a tree with strong roots that no wind can knock down.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says:
If there is no Torah,
there are no good manners.
If there are no good manners,
there is no Torah.
If there is no wisdom,
there is no fear of Hashem.
If there is no fear of Hashem,
there is no wisdom.
If there is no understanding,
there is no knowledge.
If there is no knowledge,
there is no understanding.
If there is no flour,
chunks.explain: Without food, a person cannot learn.

chunks.en: there is no Torah.
If there is no Torah,
there is no flour.
He used to say:
Anyone whose wisdom is more than his deeds,
what is he like?
Like a tree with many branches and few roots,

chunks.he: וְהָרוּחַ בָּאָה וְעוֹקַרְתּוֹ וְהוֹפַכְתּוֹ עַל פָּנָיו,
chunks.en: and the wind comes and pulls it up and turns it over on its face,
as it says (Yirmiyah 17): And he will be like a lonely bush in the desert,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי יָבוֹא טוֹב וְשָׁכַן
chunks.en: and he will not see when good comes, and he will live

chunks.he: חֲרֵרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶרֶץ מְלֵחָה וְלֹא תֵשֵׁב.
chunks.en: in dry places in the wilderness, a salty land where no one lives.
But anyone whose deeds are more than his wisdom,
what is he like?
Like a tree with few branches and many roots,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כָל הָרוּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם בָּאוֹת וְנוֹשְׁבוֹת
chunks.en: that even if all the winds in the world come and blow
at it, they cannot move it from its place,
as it says (there): And he will be like a tree planted by

chunks.he: מַיִם וְעַל יוּבַל יְשַׁלַּח שָׁרָשָׁיו וְלֹא
chunks.en: the water, that sends its roots by a stream, and will not
see when heat comes,
and its leaves will be fresh,
and in a year of no rain it will not worry,
and it will not stop making fruit.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Chisma teaches that even hard, detailed laws are the main body of halachah, while counting the seasons and number puzzles are like extras around wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Chisma says:
The laws of bird korbanos and the laws of niddah,

words.note: Laws about a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: they are the main body of the halachos.
Counting the seasons and number counting

words.note: Counting the times of the sun and moon.

chunks.en: are the side dishes of wisdom.
